## Available development release

[**v0.4.0-preview.2**](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/releases/tag/v0.4.0-preview.2)
provides checked Linux x86-64 (glibc 2.35+) and Windows x86-64 binaries.
No Rust compilation is needed. [Install that explicit version](install.qmd);
GitHub's stable Latest remains the older v0.3.0.

This development prerelease delivers M1: a useful local CLI preview.
The table summarizes supported Rust CLI behavior; it does not establish R/IDE parity. See the
[detailed status](preview-status.qmd) and [delivery evidence](release-delivery.qmd)
for exact verification and limits. Newer changes on main need their own evidence.

| Capability | What it means for you |
|---|---|
| Choose the project | `--project PATH` selects the folder for a command. Child queries retain that root. |
| Preview an analysis | `build-dev` runs your selected steps without CLI version changes, output promotion or archive export. |
| Read without changing files | Configuration validation and path queries do not create target folders or edit ignore files. |
| Detect command failures | Errors produce a nonzero exit status, so an automated run can stop. |
| Run without questions | `--non-interactive` disables CLI prompts and automatic package installation, and closes runner input. |
| Select no analysis | An explicit `scripts: []` runs no analysis scripts. Hooks may still run; production can export existing outputs. |
| Run scripts and render documents | The build engine supports Python, R, Quarto and R Markdown/Bookdown targets, with the corresponding tools installed. |
| Keep a local output archive | Production builds can export configured outputs to local content-addressed storage, which avoids storing identical content repeatedly. |

### Preview has a boundary

The CLI skips its own release operations during a preview, including cleanup
of released outputs and prior caches. **This is not a filesystem sandbox.**
Scripts, hooks and renderers can still change files. Generated-output path queries default to the selected versioned cache. Use those
paths from your scripts, as in the [tutorial](tutorial.qmd); arbitrary writes are
still outside that rule.

Document renderers have their own working folders and output rules.
Mixed-language scheduling is not a promise that every target runs in the exact
order written in configuration. See the [build reference](cli/build.qmd) for
the current implementation and the [behavior contract](behavior.qmd) for limits.

## Known limits of the published preview

- A preview is not a filesystem sandbox. Scripts and hooks control their writes;
  automatic redirection of every renderer's output is not provided.
- Matching results and paths across CLI runs, RStudio and GUI rendering has not
  been proved.
- Complete compatibility with every `projr` workflow has not been established.
- Mixed script and document targets do not have a complete sequential-order
  guarantee.
- This preview supplies only Linux and Windows x86-64 binaries; macOS and ARM
  delivery are unavailable.
- Production recovery is bounded. It does not undo arbitrary script writes or
  partial external publication effects.

The existing R package is unchanged. A Rust library is available in this
repository, but new R, Python and Julia frontend integrations are separate work.

## Planned work

M2 and later milestones remain unfinished. Complete input/code/config/dependency
provenance, durable attempt/release records and analysis-free publication retry
are separate work. General command/argv steps and stronger execution policies
remain follow-ups; they are not silently interpreted from missing script paths.

For the detailed evidence, scope and decisions, see the
[behavior contract](behavior.qmd) and [compatibility log](compatibility.qmd).

## Included in preview.2

The released CLI keeps a captured project context, defaults generated-output
queries to a safe versioned cache, and uses native working folders unless you
choose the project-folder override. It supports explicit R-package data management,
none/pre/post output cleanup, success-only output promotion and local archives.
Supported HTML defaults to embedded resources only when no effective embedding
option was supplied; explicit and inherited false remain respected.

Real acceptance covers configured/no-init and fresh directory initialization,
ordered Python/R/report steps, a computed CSV and embedded report, structured
failures and verified final/archive bytes without Git credentials. See
[the acceptance and delivery evidence](release-delivery.qmd).

Bookdown site embedding is unchanged. Existing R helpers and R/IDE parity, linked
HTML portability, complete provenance and publication retry remain outside this
claim. The [behavior contract](behavior.qmd) remains the detailed source of scope.
